chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali ibn Hadid, from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughirah al-Nasri, who said:
I heard Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام saying:

"The salat (prayer) of the daytime is sixteen rak'ahs: eight when the sun declines, and eight after al-Zuhr, and four rak'ahs after al-Maghrib. O Harith, do not leave them whether in travel or residence. And two rak'ahs after al-'Isha' al-Akhirah—my father used to perform them while sitting, and I perform them while standing. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to perform thirteen rak'ahs in the night."

key_terms.اللَّيْلِ: the night, here referring to the night prayer
key_terms.زَالَتِ: declined, referring to the sun passing the zenith
key_terms.صَلَاةُ: salat (prayer), here referring to recommended ritual prayers

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام teach about the recommended daily and nightly prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines recommended salat (prayer) units connected to the daily cycle, including daytime nawafil, the post-Maghrib prayer, the two rak'ahs after al-'Isha', and the night prayer of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It emphasizes continuity in these acts of worship in both travel and residence and preserves the practice transmitted from the Imams عليهم السلام.
